solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lap irregular yet lap time fast

parts.note: to lap is to lick, as a cat laps milk

indicators.note: irregular means out of order, so the letters of yet are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
in racing a split is the time recorded for one lap or section

explanation.surface: An athlete runs an uneven lap, yet still clocks a quick lap time.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Lap' is the verb to drink like a cat; 'lap time' is the racing term for one circuit's time.
explanation.definitionFit: Lickety-split is an informal adverb meaning very quickly, at full speed.

clue.text: Three occupying one runner's space — where to go?

indicators.note: occupying means filling a space, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: on a track each runner has a lane
tri- is the prefix meaning three

explanation.surface: Three athletes crammed into a single runner's lane, wondering where to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where to go?' is a coy way of naming a toilet, not a question about direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A latrine is a basic toilet, the place one goes to relieve oneself.

clue.text: Organised judge has food brought up outside

indicators.note: outside means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: cud is food a cow brings up from its stomach to chew again
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A judge who is organised has his meal brought up to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' looks like a reversal signal, but it is part of the definition of cud, regurgitated food.
explanation.definitionFit: A curated collection has been selected and organised, as by a museum keeper.

clue.text: Guy's dead upset, I state from experience

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read in the opposite direction

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is written of the dead
Guy is the setter, so Guy's = Guy is = ME
taken as written
CAL is an abbreviation of California, a US state

explanation.surface: The setter laments being upset to death, stating his view from experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy's' is 'Guy is': the setter Guy refers to himself, and 'upset' turns the setter-plus-dead pair upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Empirical knowledge is based on observation and practical evidence rather than theory.

clue.text: They run until they get too hot

definitions.text: They run until they get too hot

parts.words: They run until they get too hot
parts.note: runny egg centres stay liquid until cooking sets them firm

explanation.surface: Sounds like runners who keep going until they overheat.
explanation.walkthrough: The running track theme suggests athletes; the things that run are the soft centres of eggs, which set when heated.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg centres are liquid when soft-boiled and harden with more heat, so they run only until cooked.

clue.text: How dead mop might be treated?

definitions.text: How dead mop might be treated?

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking how to revive a lifeless head of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: a lank mop of hair could be dressed with pomade.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomaded hair has been dressed with scented grease, a treatment for lifeless hair.

clue.text: Some of quartet are Tippexing over repeat

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the letters are turned back to front
some of means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the run ETARETI sits across these words

explanation.surface: Members of a quartet blanking out a repeat mark with correction fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some of' picks ETARETI from quartET ARE TIppexing, and 'over' turns it round. Tipp-Ex is a British brand of correction fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do or say again, a synonym of the verb repeat.

clue.text: Coe keeps running manic laps, going along with others

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Sebastian Coe, Olympic champion, taken as written

indicators.note: running suggests something in motion, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Seb Coe keeps running frantic laps alongside the other athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian Coe is a British middle-distance runner, double Olympic 1500m champion; his name is used as plain letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaisance is a willingness to please, a readiness to agree with and accommodate others.

clue.text: Rock up with unfashionable hairstyle

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
a crop is a short haircut

explanation.surface: Someone turns up with a dated haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock up' is British slang for arriving; only 'Rock' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is a mass of bedrock that shows above the surrounding ground.

clue.text: Predict hospital's on strike in London borough

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after, so these pieces come after the strike

parts.note: to lam is to hit hard
to bet is to predict, as in 'I bet it rains'
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Forecasting that hospital staff are going on strike in a London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambeth is an inner borough of London, on the south bank of the Thames.

clue.text: Part of lap showing Olympic 800m champion's quality, in commentary

indicators.note: commentary is spoken, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: Kelly Holmes won 800m gold at Athens 2004; her quality is a Holmes trait

explanation.surface: A race commentator describes the closing stretch and the champion's attribute.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Kelly Holmes is a British runner who won the 800m and 1500m at the 2004 Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: The home straight is the final stretch of a racetrack before the finishing line.

clue.text: Signpost to Bury showing parking for the first time

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another, here at the start

parts.note: taken as written
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
to inter is to bury a body

explanation.surface: A sign for Bury, the Lancashire town, displays a parking symbol for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parking for the first time' means P replaces the T at the start of TO, giving PO.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer indicates a direction, as a signpost does.

clue.text: Weapon made by Siemens, thought marines

parts.note: S is the symbol for the siemens, the SI unit of conductance
an idea is a thought
RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A gun manufactured by the German firm Siemens, the marines believed.
explanation.walkthrough: Siemens is also a unit of electrical conductance, symbol S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidearm is a small weapon, such as a pistol, worn at the side.

clue.text: Change the last word and the first in dictionary

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer, its final word

indicators.note: the first in means the opening letter is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor alters the last word and the first word in a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to alter or correct, a verb synonym of change.

clue.text: Conservative, flashy and not so uniformly blue

parts.note: loud means garish or flashy
less means not so much

explanation.surface: A Tory who is showy and not so true blue, the party colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the Conservative colour, but here 'uniformly blue' describes a sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloudless sky is blue all over, with no patches of white or grey.

clue.text: Short race involved team with one carrying a baton

definitions.text: team with one carrying a baton

indicators.note: involved means tangled or intricate, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sprint relay team in which a runner carries the baton.
explanation.walkthrough: The baton suggests a relay; it is a conductor's stick.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a group of musicians led by a conductor who wields a baton.

clue.text: Disorganised mob has woolly Liberal in charge

indicators.note: woolly means muddled or confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chaotic crowd is led by a muddle-headed Liberal politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Shambolic is informal British for chaotic and badly organised.

clue.text: Violent crime holding Oliver's axe

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ABH is actual bodily harm, a British criminal offence
Oli is short for Oliver, so Oliver's gives OLIS

explanation.surface: A violent attack in which Oliver's axe is seized.
explanation.walkthrough: ABH, actual bodily harm, is a common assault charge in British law.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe something is to cut or scrap it, as a government might abolish a policy.

clue.text: Direction in which Russian icon laps circuit

indicators.note: laps here means overlaps, so the two words share their common letter

parts.note: the bear is the national symbol of Russia
a ring is a circuit

explanation.surface: Asking which way a famous Russian runs around the track.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAR overlaps RING on their shared R, so the R is counted once: BEA + RING.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearing is a compass direction measured from a fixed point.

clue.text: Huge Bentley, perhaps a director's desideratum

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a Bentley is an example of a car

explanation.surface: A grand Bentley as the luxury a company boss covets.
explanation.walkthrough: The director here is a film director, not a company one.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar is the Academy Award, the prize a film director most wants.

clue.text: Wrong virgin brought over for sacrifice

parts.note: off means bad or wrong, as in off milk

indicators.note: brought over in a down clue means turned upward, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: virgin means pure, untouched

explanation.surface: A wrongly chosen virgin is carried across to be sacrificed.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer up is to present something as an offering, as in a sacrifice to a god.

clue.text: Flyer is able to control flipping

parts.note: can means is able to

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to rein is to control, as with a horse

explanation.surface: A pilot is able to control a plane as it flips over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' is not a pilot but 'more fly', fly being slang for shrewd.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly is informal for streetwise, so flyer means more shrewd, like cannier.

clue.text: Gas had child out for a short time

definitions.text: child out for a short time

parts.note: neon is a noble gas
had a meal means ate

explanation.surface: Someone who had a child went outside briefly because of a gas leak.
explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn infant, one who has only recently left the womb.

clue.text: Quits rugby after having head knocked off

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: sevens is a short form of rugby union with seven a side

explanation.surface: A player gives up rugby after being knocked on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits means being even, with nothing owed either way.

clue.text: Turkish gent forces butt into denim regularly

indicators.note: into means put inside another piece
regularly means taking every other letter

parts.note: taken as written; its second and fourth letters are taken
F is the physics abbreviation for force, so forces is FF
a butt is the end of something, as a cigarette butt

explanation.surface: Physical force drives a rear end into regular denim jeans.
explanation.definitionFit: Effendi is a Turkish title of respect for a man of education or standing.

clue.text: Building over in the city provided fish

indicators.note: over means turned the other way, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
if means provided that
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A city construction delivered fish across town.
explanation.walkthrough: ECIFIDE read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing building.

clue.text: Lake sort of muddy

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
-ish means somewhat or sort of

explanation.surface: Describing a lake as rather murky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddy' looks like an adjective but is a verb, to stain or sully.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish a reputation is to sully or dirty it.

clue.text: American's funny story of one doing lap after lap?

indicators.note: after means this piece is placed following the other one

parts.note: your lap is the tops of your thighs when seated
a lapper is one who laps, whether a runner or a drinker

explanation.surface: An American gag about a runner completing lap after lap.
explanation.walkthrough: The running theme suggests circuits, but the second lap is the seated lap, the thighs.
explanation.definitionFit: A thigh-slapper is a uproarious joke, so funny it makes hearers slap their legs.
